bluf: JVWEB is a French paid media specialist selling search, social and display ads with SEO and GEO to a mixed book it claims runs to 500+ active clients across 40+ countries on 22 years of experience. Its AI move is public: a GEO page with its VIA dashboard, a Data & AI lab building ad platform automations, and 22 AI topic URLs in its sitemap. The record holds no moves, news, jobs or named clients. Its own house practises 1 of 4 tested lines: it sells AI visibility with no llms.txt, sells paid social with no social pixel, and sells LinkedIn demand with 0 LinkedIn ads.
doing:
JVWEB positions as a profitable growth digital marketing agency orchestrating search, social and display ads with SEO and GEO, pitching talent led, data driven acquisition: it buys ads across Google, Microsoft, the social platforms and display, and adds organic and AI visibility around the buying. Its headline claim is 500+ active clients across 40+ countries, backed by 22 years of experience; the record holds the claim and names none of them.

The sold mix leads with paid search and paid social, both scored 3. Search Ads is the first homepage lever (Google Ads, Shopping, Microsoft) and SEA leads the nav; the social lever spans Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Snapchat, TikTok and Pinterest. Four core lines score 2: AI Automation on a Data & AI lab that builds custom tools and ad platform automations; AI Search / GEO on a dedicated GEO page with the VIA dashboard, a five step mention rate method and a GEO white paper; Programmatic & CTV on a display lever covering programmatic, video, DOOH, YouTube and native; SEO on audits, migration, technical, content and netlinking. The service list adds Amazon Ads, Netlinking, Créa and the Pôle Data & IA. Proprietary lines are VIA (tracking brand visibility in AI answers), the lab itself, and Seiso, Inspecto and Radar, nav items beside VIA whose functions are not shown; no partner badges are listed.

Its AI posture is concrete: GEO sold through VIA and a five step test method, an in house lab feeding automations into ad platforms, and 22 AI search URLs including ChatGPT Ads Manager in France. The record lists no dated moves, no news, no case studies, no jobs and no pricing signals. Conspicuously absent for a paid media specialist of 22 years: a single named client, an office list, ownership, headcount, and any audited output from VIA (citation share, scorecard, tracking) that would turn the dashboard into a product a buyer can check.
clients:
The record reads the client type as mixed and the verticals as ecommerce, fashion, education, travel and B2B; the home market is France, with no office list. The needs read holds 0 clients: no case study, no logo, no press release and no slug names an account, so nothing is observed, nothing is named only and nothing is shared with another tracked agency. Set against a headline claim of 500+ active clients across 40+ countries, that silence is the finding: the book is asserted as a number and never shown as names, and a rival cannot contest a named account from this record because there is none.

What the base needs next is inferred from the sold mix, since no client signal exists. Advertisers buying search, social and display through a specialist sit under KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer), the judgment the Horus read marks JVWEB most exposed to through its two lead lines, and under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), the one it is best placed for through its GEO line. It is likely, low confidence, that the ecommerce and fashion accounts will move buying hours into platform automation and ask the agency for the inputs instead, which the P4 read says the record does not yet show; it is likely, moderate confidence, that the same accounts will ask for the mention rate VIA promises before they renew the media retainer.
house: Say and do: four lines tested, one practised, integrity 25. AI search is contradicted: it sells AI visibility and publishes no llms.txt, while carrying 22 AI topic URLs in a 156 URL sitemap. Paid social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel on its own site. LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: it sells paid social and B2B demand generation and the Ad Library returns 0 ads (the note reads '0 ads match the name query (all advertisers); first results page shows 0 cards'). Paid search is unknown because the Transparency Center lookup was blocked. Publishing cadence is recorded as corroborated on 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 6 in 365, a cadence of almost nothing. The house runs on Webflow with GA4 and Axeptio only: no pixels, no test tools, no ABM stack. It blocks no AI crawlers. The Radar flagged three gaps: no llms.txt, no social pixel, no LinkedIn ads.
market:
Horus puts JVWEB at tailwind index 0.6, band Neutral, 16:17 on the Solar Arc. Best placed for KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation, driven by AI Search / GEO). Most exposed to KJ4 (the platforms absorbing the execution layer, driven by Paid Search and Paid Social). Best scenario fit: The Bazaar of Agents at 42/100. It is making P2 (feeds, schema or entity work alongside a core line), partial on P1, P4 and P6 (AI operator depth shows, not the full move), absent on P3, P7 and P8; P5 is unknown.

The Monsoon read is 49.6, band Breeze, percentile 26: migration 48.1 against displacement 51.1. The sold mix supplies 48 of the index, SEO (10) and Paid Search (10) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 45% to Africa and the Maghreb, 30% to South and Southeast Asia and 20% to Eastern Europe, and automation overlaps 32%. The footprint is inferred with no hub offices; the read records onshore claims in its own words, both of them the in house Data & AI lab sentences.
openings:
The strongest opening is three contradictions on one house: it sells AI visibility through VIA and publishes no llms.txt, sells paid social and runs no social pixel, sells LinkedIn demand and shows 0 LinkedIn ads. A rival that practises all three can very likely (high confidence) win the comparison in front of the ecommerce, fashion, education, travel or B2B buyers it names as verticals. Falsifier: a later compile showing an llms.txt, a social pixel and LinkedIn ads under the JVWEB name closes it.

The book is invisible: 0 named clients against a claim of 500+, so every account is open to a rival who can find it. VIA is a dashboard with no audited output on record (P1 partial), so a rival with a citation share number leads with it. Its most exposed judgment is KJ4 through both lead lines, and P4 is partial: the first party data, creative volume and measurement depth the platforms' automation consumes are the pitch against it. No public pricing (P5 unknown) leaves an outcome priced offer unanswered. Displacement at 51.1 says lead with proof, not price. The idle sitemap (0 updates in 90 days) is the symptom to raise.
watch: I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: any disclosed AI checkout GMV would deepen the KJ4 exposure of its two lead lines, and high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the paid search lead, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind its GEO page sells into.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM decide whether the ChatGPT Ads Manager it writes about in France becomes a surface it tests (P8 absent).
The blocked Transparency Center lookup: the next compile should retry it, since whether a paid search specialist runs its own Google ads is the one house test still unread.
